title: Trail Distance Estimator: Path Length on the Map
description: Compare two locations by straight-line distance; this workspace does not measure a traced trail.
summary_sentence: Straight-line distance between two endpoints can be shorter than a winding trail; this workspace does not trace the route.
quick_answer: This workspace measures the spherical great-circle distance between two points. It does not trace trails or sum multiple path segments, so the result is not a trail-length estimate.
steps_intro: Choose two locations by searching or clicking the map, then read their straight-line distance. Use a suitable route or track tool for an actual path.

body.t: A straight-line endpoint distance can provide context for a hike, but it does not account for the actual trail or elevation.
Race course length requires the actual path and a suitable measurement method, not just its two endpoints.
For trail signage, measure the route between junctions with a suitable track or survey workflow; this workspace only measures endpoints.
Compare endpoint distance with a published trail length only as a rough context, not an independent trail measurement.
A winding trail can be longer than the shortest surface distance between its endpoints. Measuring that trail requires its route, not only the endpoints.
A horizontal map measurement does not account for elevation changes. Terrain and the route taken can affect the distance travelled.

popular_table.title: What this workspace measures
popular_table.intro: Choose the measurement that fits the task.
popular_table.note: The displayed result uses a spherical great-circle approximation and does not follow trails or roads.

faq: Can this measure a drawn trail?
No. It measures straight-line distance between two locations, not a drawn or uploaded trail.
No. Elevation and terrain are not included.
Can it measure a road route?
No. It does not follow roads; use a routing tool for road-network distances.
The calculation is a spherical great-circle approximation. Location input accuracy and the chosen earth model affect the result.
